subject: SCIENCE
title: Animals Around Us
objective: Relate familiar animals to suitable habitats without disturbing wildlife.
introduction: A fish lives in water and a bird builds a nest in a tree. Where do animals call home?

vocabulary.definition: The liquid all living things need.
A safe place that protects living things.
A living thing that can move and needs food.

items.prompt: Which statement about habitats is true?

options.text: Habitats provide resources such as food, water, shelter, and space.
Every animal fits one habitat only

items.explanation: A habitat gives animals food, water, shelter, and space. Many animals use Animals Around Us habitat, and wild animals should stay in the wild.

items.prompt: Which example shows a suitable habitat?
items.explanation: Fish need water to live, so a water habitat suits them. Trees and deserts cannot give fish what they need.

items.prompt: Which statement is not true?  (in this lesson: Animals Around Us)

options.text: Every animal fits one habitat only

items.explanation: Many animals use different habitats for different needs, so no animal fits only one habitat. Birds do nest, and fish do live in water.

items.prompt: Why does an animal need a habitat?

options.text: It changes every animal into a pet.
It gives the animal a school grade.

items.explanation: A habitat gives an animal the food, water, shelter, and space it needs to live. It does not give grades or turn animals into pets.
Frogs need a moist place, so a moist habitat suits them. Hot desert sand and the deep ocean floor are too dry or too far.

assetSpecs.prompt: Friendly Grade 3 cartoon storybook concept board for Animals Around Us; rounded shapes, warm dark-brown outlines, tropical palette, no embedded text, uncluttered small-screen layout. Compose overlays provide labels and interactive targets.

safetyNotes: Use the on-screen activity only; no unsupervised physical experiment is required.
